setting.name: Nonpaged Pool Size
setting.casual_explanation: Nonpaged pool is kernel memory that must always stay resident in RAM. This is a low-level legacy tuning area that normal users should not adjust manually.
setting.why_people_change_it: People only touch it when undoing old memory tweaks or investigating unusual kernel memory issues on older systems.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The app only writes the documented reset value 0. This is still a legacy low-level area, but the current implementation is a reset-to-default action rather than a custom tuning value.
setting.professional_notes: Microsoft Q&A now captures NonPagedPoolSize = 0 as part of the default Memory Management registry snapshot. The current app writes NonPagedPoolSize = 0 under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management, matching that default reset value. That makes the current app behavior an exact reset-to-default mapping, not an unsupported custom pool-size override.

evidence.title: KVM ETW summary receipt for NonPagedPoolSize
evidence.summary: A bounded 2026-04-27 ETW retry for `NonPagedPoolSize` never reached trace collection. QGA guest-exec failed during guest-dir setup, the runner fell back to send-key launch, and the fallback still timed out in `ensure-admin-shell` before any ETW artifact reached the host.

evidence.title: QGA-first ETW stackwalk runtime receipt for NonPagedPoolSize
evidence.summary: A 2026-05-07 QGA-first ETW stackwalk rerun produced ETL/XML artifacts and normalized 4389 registry events with 527 caller-stack events. The bundle contains an exact helper-triggered `RegQueryValue` for `HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Session Manager\Memory Management` / `NonPagedPoolSize`, returning `0x80000005` on the clean baseline.

evidence.title: Guest Ghidra launch receipt for NonPagedPoolSize
evidence.summary: A same-day fast guest Ghidra retry for `NonPagedPoolSize` failed in `ensure-admin-shell` with a bounded timeout, so no xref bundle reached the host.

decision.why: Microsoft Q&A captures NonPagedPoolSize = 0 as the default Memory Management value, the app writes that same reset value exactly, and restore support is already in place. This stays legacy and low-level, but the current app action is an exact reset-to-default mapping and is safe to expose.
